target_customer: IT, HR and operations teams at companies using Microsoft Teams and Slack
problem: Internal requests and approvals are buried in email, shared inboxes and chat threads; Jetdocs provides ticketing with workflows inside Teams and Slack.

founders.name: Andrew Dolinski
previous_startups: Clutch.ca (co-founder and COO, per YC page; exited, per Accelerator Centre)

founders.name: Alex Kovalev
founders.background_notes: Full stack web developer per the YC page.

competitors.name: atSpoke
competitors.what: Slack based internal ticketing and help desk

competitors.name: Jira
competitors.what: General issue tracking that companies stretched to internal requests

technical_complexity.rationale: Chat integrations and workflow builder with tickets and approvals, standard SaaS engineering for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Workflows embedded in a company's processes create some lock-in, but many competitors and the chat platforms themselves can copy features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it; Jetdocs now builds on Microsoft Teams with an AI assistant.

market_need_then: Founders said the problem came from sharing information across departments; the company says teams drown in email chains and shared inboxes.

identity.logo: Jetdocs logo and Gerald assistant logo
identity.mascot_or_character: Gerald, an AI assistant that works inside Teams

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests documents rather than ticketing and is confusable with similar Jet names; the Gerald assistant is a small branding asset.

outcome_analysis: Jetdocs is still active with a live site, SOC 2 Type II and a Teams AI assistant named Gerald, but the YC page lists a team of two. No funding amount was verified, so the funding trajectory is unknown rather than zero. The stalled visible growth suggests a small bootstrapped business, though no source states this.
notes: Unverified aggregator figures: CB Insights lists $130K dated 2022-08-04 and about $260K total; PitchBook lists $3M. The 2021 round is from the Accelerator Centre article (Feb 2025) saying first venture funding came after YC with an undisclosed amount. Jira source is dated 2025, not at founding. The atSpoke comparison page is undated. Clutch.ca role is from the YC page; do not confuse with Clutch Technologies.
